name: Bello v Attorney-General of Oyo State
summary: A right-to-life and due-process case arising from the execution of a convict while an appeal was still pending.
facts: A condemned prisoner was executed while his appeal remained pending. The estate/representatives challenged the execution as unlawful.
issues: Whether executing a convict while an appeal is pending violates the right to life and fair process.
What duty the State owes once appellate process has been invoked.
holding: The case is remembered for condemning the execution of a person while appeal processes that could affect the conviction/sentence were still live. Students must verify the precise ratio in the law report.
ratio: Where appellate process is pending, the State must not render the appeal nugatory by carrying out the death sentence; doing so engages the constitutional protection of life and due process.
report_citation: See NWLR / law-report citation via a licensed law-report service

interpretations.body: Connect this case to s.33 (right to life) and s.36 (fair hearing). Discuss the relationship between capital punishment authorised by law and the procedural protections that must still be respected.
